text: I called my son's ex-wife during his wedding, and I don't regret it. See, I didn't think I'd fit into my dress for my son's wedding, and his fiance Taylor made sure I knew it too. So at their engagement party last February, she pulled me aside and said, Linda, the wedding's in June. That's only four months. Do you think you'll have time to, you know, slim down a bit before photos? I just stared at her and she explained, it's just that Jacob mentioned you've been struggling with your weight since menopause, and I want everyone to look their best. And Lord knows I was already eating clean and working out four times a week, but the belly fat wouldn't budge no matter what I tried. So I called my ex-daughter-in-law Bailey that night, Jacob's first wife. We stayed close after the divorce, and I told her what Taylor said. That's disgusting, Bailey said, but Linda, just get new aura. I'm serious. Watch this video about menopause belly fat. I'm sending it now. Bailey does model fittings. She's going to shoots and fittings every week. So I watched what she sent, and it explained that when estrogen drops after menopause, a gut bacteria called acromantia dies off. And acromantia keeps the gut lining sealed tight. So when it dies, the gut gets tiny holes in it, and undigested food and toxins leak into the bloodstream, triggering inflammation. And because the gut can't absorb nutrients properly, the body thinks it's starving and panics, spiking cortisol and storing more fat around the abdomen because this area has four times the cortisol receptors than anywhere else. So it wasn't the carbs, but my gut lining leaking toxins. And the video went on to say berberine regrows acromantia by telling the gut to make the protective layer again. So the bacteria has food and can grow back to seal the gut lining. But berberine doesn't absorb well on its own because the gut blocks 99% of it. So black pepper extract fixes this and lets 20 times more absorb. Then Bailey texted me a link to something called new aura, which read, they have both. I've been using it for years. So I ordered it expecting another letdown, but that was mid February. And by week three, my jeans felt a little looser in the morning. By week five, the belly that stuck out started flattening. And by week eight, I went down a whole dress size. So the wedding was June 15th and I wore a fitted navy dress size eight, same size I wore before menopause hit. Taylor saw me at the rehearsal dinner the night before and her face went completely blank. Then she smiled that tight smile and said, Linda, you look great. What did you do? Just fixed my gut bacteria. I said, she blinked, you're what? Acromantia. It's the bacteria that dies during menopause. I re-grew it. She had no idea what to say to that. And at the wedding the next day, I didn't hide in the back of the group shot, but stood right next to her. And later that evening, Taylor's aunt pulled me aside during cocktail hour and said, you look incredible. Taylor mentioned you lost weight about 25 pounds since February. How? I've been trying everything. So I told her about Acromantia, about the berberine and black pepper. She pulled out her phone and asked me to send her the link. And Taylor walked past right as her aunt was typing new aura into her browser. And I caught her eye and smiled because smart women don't starve themselves to fit someone else's timeline. They just figure out what's actually broken and fix it. So next time someone makes you feel like your menopause belly is your fault. Just know it's not. It's your gut asking for help, but now you know exactly what to give it.
